title: Avoid Using Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Drain Lines
description: A frequent installation error in residential drainage systems is installing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal waste pipe transition. Sanitary tees are engineered specifically to direct water from horizontal branches into vertical stacks. When installed horizontally, the short radius curve fails to sweep waste smoothly, leading to standing solids, frequent clogs, and sluggish flow. For horizontal drain connections, plumbing codes mandate using a long-turn combination wye and 1/8 bend or a standard wye with a 45-degree elbow to maintain proper flow velocity and prevent blockages.

Avoid Using Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Drain Lines

A frequent installation error in residential drainage systems is installing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal waste pipe transition. Sanitary tees are engineered specifically to direct water from horizontal branches into vertical stacks. When installed horizontally, the short radius curve fails to sweep waste smoothly, leading to standing solids, frequent clogs, and sluggish flow. For horizontal drain connections, plumbing codes mandate using a long-turn combination wye and 1/8 bend or a standard wye with a 45-degree elbow to maintain proper flow velocity and prevent blockages.
